zoe: quick follow-up from RFC sync — idea to publish both a blob-level cipher_id and a model-level manifest_id so loaders can decide dedupe semantics.

farid: can you clarify difference?

zoe: cipher_id = hash(ciphertext) after whatever encryption/wrapping applied. manifest_id = hash(canonicalized model weights + canonical metadata (version,tokenspec)).

megan: who computes manifest_id if publisher never sees plaintext? e.g. customer-supplied key.

zoe: packager should compute manifest_id when it has plaintext; if not available, publish cipher_id only and mark manifest_id=null. registry returns whichever is present.

farid: streaming verify plan: if cipher_id present and matches mirror -> do incremental hash while piping to GPU; if only manifest_id present -> stream-decrypt-into-verifier (requires holding AE tag until end) or fallback to disk. both options need careful backpressure.

megan: add fields: chunk_size, chunk_checksums (optional), plaintext_fingerprint, ciphertext_fingerprint, bloom_opt_in flag. manifest remains additive.

infra-bot: ticket INF-8200 created: manifest-v2-fingerprint-fields.

zoe: tests: cipher_dedupe_fastpath, decrypt_then_verify, bloom_privacy_controls, origin_fallback_metrics. telemetry: dedupe_hits, stream_verify_failures, origin_switches.

megan: rollout: additive fields -> registry stores for new publishes -> canary loaders opt-in to cipher dedupe -> enable for mirrors that guarantee identical ciphertext.

farid: note: we should not do cross-shard chunk dedupe in v1. scope creep.

zoe: agreed. i'll draft short RFC patch and link INF-8200.

megan: +1

farid: +1. will prototype incremental blake3 wrapper.

infra-bot: INF-8200 linked to RFC-391.
